newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says hunting killer of U.S. businessman.
newsitem.headline: Russia says hunting killer of U.S. businessman.

text.p: Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Wednesday his services were doing all they could to find the murderer of U.S. businessman Paul Tatum, who was gunned down by an unknown assassin on a Moscow street on Sunday.

Tatum, 39, from Oklahoma, was shot with a automatic rifle on Sunday as he entered the Kievskaya metro station, in front of the Radisson-Slavjanskaya hotel over whose ownership he had been locked in litigation for several years.
"We will do all we can to uncover this criminal," Kulikov told a news conference, saying his investigators were reporting to him twice a day on their progress.
Tatum's shooting shocked the foreign business community in a city where gangland slaying are commonplace but the murder of business people from the West was unheard of until now.
Kulikov suggested various possible motives for the killing, saying one version was that it was linked to the hotel dispute.
Tatum had been fighting a legal battle with Moscow city authorities over control of the Radisson, which opened in 1991.

But the minister also said it could have been designed to humiliate the police and promote instability as Russian President Boris Yeltsin underwent open heart surgery and the United States held a presidential election.
"I do not exclude the aim of destabilising the situation and showing the inability of the forces of law and order," Kulikov told the news conference, organised by Interfax news agency.
